svg.title: The Transatlantic Slave Trade & The Middle Passage (1619–1807)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of the Atlantic Basin (1619–1807) illustrating all three legs of the Transatlantic Triangular Trade: British slave-trading ports (Liverpool, Bristol, London), West African coastal forts and kingdoms (Elmina, Cape Coast Castle, Bight of Biafra), the horrific Middle Passage across the Atlantic (Brookes and 1781 Zong), Caribbean sugar islands (Jamaica, Barbados) and Thirteen Colonies (Virginia, Charleston), and return cargoes of slave-produced sugar, tobacco, and cotton.

text.tspan: Elmina, Cape Coast & Biafra; Royal African Co.

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: THE FIRST BRITISH EMPIRE (1600–1783)
The Transatlantic Slave Trade & The Middle Passage (1619–1807)
Between 1619 and 1807, British ships forced ~3.1 million Africans onto the Middle Passage to work Caribbean & American plantations.
Slave-grown sugar, tobacco, and cotton enriched British ports and banks until resistance, Equiano, and abolitionists won the 1807 ban.
